parsed.explanation: The combined regime layers a federal document regime (markers only M/F, X-bar, discrepancy-refusal and possible lifetime fraud ineligibility, travellers stranded) onto a state with a K-12 facility ban, a minor-present public-facility misdemeanour, an arrest-and-birth-sex-custody precedent in an analogous state, religiously-permitted care denial, no state discrimination or hate-crime protection, and a 'Worst Policies In Effect' grading. Federal immigration custody documents beatings, solitary and sexual abuse for trans detainees; federal prisons mandate conversion-therapy-style regimes. Litigation is active but remedies are slow and uneven; several foreign governments now warn trans travellers. No identity criminalisation, no death penalty, national hate-crime and employment protections remain. Universal document and facility exposures with thin recourse dominate.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal order and Feb 2025 cable: markers restricted to M/F, X halted, discrepancy triggers refusal and possible lifetime fraud ineligibility; travellers report confiscated/blocked passports and stranding. Universal, inescapable exposure at every document check.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid to expiry; fraud finding requires four elements with limited waiver and is never automatic; ACLU suit pending; legal-aid FAQ guides document strategy.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy can escalate to refusal, fraud allegation, then detention or birth-sex placement in any facility downstream.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal immigration custody documents forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse of trans detainees; federal corrections since 2026 mandates conversion-therapy-style regime (haircut, hormone removal). Analogous-state arrest held a trans woman 24h in a men's ward.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Habeas and litigation channels exist; some orders enjoined; national hate-crime statute covers gender identity.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry refusal or fraud referral can move a visitor into the federal custody system where these documented harms operate.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Facility bans in 19+ state/provinces covering government buildings/schools; four states criminalise use in circumstances; this state's K-12 ban extended 2025 plus Act 619 misdemeanour where a minor is present; one documented arrest elsewhere (trespass, 60 days).
federal_state_facilities.protection: Act 619 requires intent to arouse plus refusal-to-depart for trespass; 29 states plus capital district lack bans; some states remain ban-free.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: A visitor using a restroom in a covered public building risks ejection, trespass charge and birth-sex custody as happened in the analogous case.

care_services.exposure: State law since 26 March allows practitioners to cite religious beliefs to deny care to LGBT patients, reaching an out-of-state visitor needing treatment; federal care restrictions and insurance proposals pending.
care_services.protection: National employment/equality ruling and emergency-treatment norms offer partial cover; several federal orders enjoined.
care_services.interaction: Being outed during an emergency can convert a medical visit into a refusal with limited state-level recourse.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal orders and counterterrorism language frame gender ideology as extremist-adjacent; AG directives to investigate 'gender ideology' in schools; public opinion 66% supports birth-sex document listing.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Counterterrorism text says powers will not target mere disagreement; reward criterion excludes the phrase; several orders blocked in court.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing raises outing probability and lowers the benefit of complaining when stopped.

minors_guardians.exposure: Parent travelling with a trans minor faces school-facility bans, criminal exposure for teachers facilitating social transition, state care ban (currently enjoined but litigated), and Act 619's minor-present trigger; DOJ subpoenaed youth medical records.
minors_guardians.protection: National judge enjoined the care ban for 'irreparable harm' during litigation; constitutional challenges continue.
minors_guardians.interaction: A family's documents or a minor's presentation can trigger facility rules and investigation simultaneously.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state hate-crime enhancement or civil remedy covering gender identity; state 2021 hate-crime law explicitly excludes it; only national statute covers GI. State lacks public-accommodation protections.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime act covers gender identity since 2009; national bias-crime statistics are recorded; municipalities bar GI discrimination in public employment.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Street incidents get thinner state-level response, pushing recourse onto slower federal mechanisms.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Enforcement of Act 619's misdemeanour here is undocumented; whether this state adopts document-invalidation or bounty regimes is unknown; whether its facility ban reaches adult government buildings is unstated; federal litigation unresolved, so exposure shifts by travel date.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Active suits (passport policy, executive orders), legal-aid FAQ, national equality/identity-document maps, working federal courts granting some injunctions.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Uncertainty itself raises risk: a traveller cannot know at booking which rules will be operative or enforced.

anchor_checks.comparison: Karthovia's pattern is routine police identity checks, hours-long interviews and vague bylaw fines with no imprisonment. This dossier is worse on custody: a documented analogous-state arrest with 24-hour men's-ward holding, a live misdemeanour statute, and documented federal immigration-custody abuse. It is better on pervasive street harassment, which is not documented here. Net: slightly below 0.35-B.

Vesskar's routine verification exposure at checkpoints, uncommon prosecutions, narrow anti-discrimination claim and scarce legal aid closely match the federal document regime here. This dossier adds criminal misdemeanour exposure, religious care denial, absent state protections and custodial abuse, pushing below 0.45-A; both share universal document exposure with uncertain escalation.

Krestrel Isles offers only administrative refusal, return transport and slow appeals — no custody harm, no facility criminalisation, no care denial. This regime documents custody abuse, birth-sex placement, criminal misdemeanours and universal marker restriction, and is materially worse than 0.55-B.

Brayelia/Qorinda-style 0.65 cases have working courts, apologies, compensation and no credible detention. Here remedies are contested and slow, state-level recourse is absent, and detention with birth-sex placement is documented. Well below 0.65-C.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller faces a two-level regime: federal document rules make gender-marker exposure universal and inescapable (refusal, fraud referral, stranding), and can funnel a discrepancy into immigration custody where abuse of trans detainees is documented. The state adds facility restrictions, a minor-present misdemeanour, religious care denial, and no state discrimination or hate-crime recourse — placing it in the 'Worst Policies In Effect' tier just below 'Do Not Travel'. A documented analogous arrest with men's-ward holding shows the birth-sex custody pathway is real, not hypothetical. Mitigation is real but partial: national hate-crime and employment protections, active litigation producing some injunctions, and no identity criminalisation or death penalty keep this out of the lowest tiers, while thin, uneven remedies hold it below mid-scale.
